title: Living in the city or the country

match.reason: The bank point teaches economic and service links between rural and urban places in Geography, not how rural or urban location affects access to sport through distance, facilities, cost and choice, so it is a different idea.

draft.title: Living in the city or the country
card: Where a person lives can affect which sports they can play. Rural and urban areas often differ in distance, facilities, cost and choice.
Distance
in the country, training and games may mean long drives. This takes time and money, and some young people cannot get a lift.
Facilities
cities usually have more pools, indoor courts and gyms close by. Small towns may have fewer venues, and some sports may not be offered at all.
Cost and choice
travel, fuel and time away from home can add to the cost of playing in the country. Cities usually offer more sports to pick from, but a town may have a strong local club that brings people together.
draft.remember: Distance, facilities, cost and choice can differ between city and country, and these differences can affect who gets to play.

a.q: Which difference between rural and urban areas can make it harder for a country teenager to play sport?
opts: Long travel to training and games
Fewer people who enjoy sport
Less interest in local clubs
Cheaper entry fees at all venues
a.why: Long travel takes time and money, and some teenagers cannot get a lift. The card does not say country people like sport less. It says distance, facilities, cost and choice differ.
a.clue: Think about how far a family may have to drive.

b.q: Priya lives in a small town in north-west Victoria. She wants to join a swimming squad, but the nearest indoor pool is two hours away. Which reason best explains why she may not be able to take part?
opts: Distance and facilities limit her access
Swimming costs less in country areas
Cities offer a smaller choice of sports
Her town has too many sports clubs
b.why: The nearest pool is far away, so distance and facilities limit what Priya can do. Travel also adds cost. The other options reverse the pattern, as cities usually offer more choice, not less.
b.clue: Look at how far the pool is and what the town lacks.

a.best: Long travel to training and games

b.best: Distance and facilities limit her access

problems.detail: The clue 'Think about how far a family may have to drive' points straight at 'Long travel to training and games'. The other options are also plainly implausible, so a Year 11 student can answer without knowing the idea.
The clue 'Look at how far the pool is and what the town lacks' matches the words of the right option 'Distance and facilities limit her access', which gives the answer away.

a.q: Which statement about sport in rural and urban areas is accurate?
opts: Country travel can add to the cost of playing
Cities usually have fewer venues close by
Small towns usually offer more sports to choose from
Country towns cannot have strong local clubs
a.why: Travel, fuel and time away from home can make country sport cost more. The options about venues and choice reverse the pattern, since cities usually have more of both. A town may still have a strong local club.
a.clue: Compare what cities and towns usually have more of.

b.q: Priya lives in a small town in north-west Victoria. She wants to join a swimming squad, but the nearest indoor pool is two hours away. Which reason best explains why she may not be able to take part?
opts: The venue she needs is a long way from home
Country squads charge higher fees to join
Country teenagers have less interest in swimming
Cities usually offer fewer squads to choose from
b.why: Her town lacks an indoor pool, so she would face long drives that take time and money. Higher joining fees may seem likely, but the scenario says nothing about fees, and the card links extra country costs to travel. Priya also wants to swim, so lack of interest does not fit.
b.clue: Use only the facts the scenario gives about Priya.
